analysis.session_summary: The tape was broadly USD-positive: USD was the strongest major at +0.271%, while JPY (-0.282%) and NZD (-0.236%) lagged. Most legs had no clear single catalyst, but the Saudi oil-cargo and East-West pipeline headline lifted Brent +2.752% and intermittently supported CAD/NOK before late NY flows took over. Treasury Secretary Bessent's remarks produced a measurable +0.044% USD impulse with high-sigma USD/CHF and USD/CAD reactions; UK jobs data was muted despite a large miss. Positioning looks long USD and short high-beta FX, with oil supply as the main cross-current.

themes.theme: Broad USD strength with JPY and NZD weakest
themes.evidence: Currency strength map: USD +0.271%, JPY -0.282%, NZD -0.236%. USD/JPY closed +0.485% at 155.067, near the top of a 124.5-pip range.

themes.theme: Oil supply shock underpins CAD and NOK against the USD tape
themes.evidence: Brent/USD closed +2.752% at 110.594, near its high (close_in_range 0.99). The Saudi cargo-cancellation headline contributed to a USD/CAD 14:30-15:45 down leg of -17.2 pips and a USD/NOK 08:30-15:45 down leg of -200.6 pips.

themes.theme: Late USD bid from Bessent remarks
themes.evidence: Treasury Sec Bessent Speaks at 16:00 produced a +0.044% USD impulse; USD/CHF +5.0 pips at 3.35 sigma, EUR/USD -3.3 pips, GBP/USD -4.2 pips.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD's -30.0 pip Asia-London slide and +20.9 pip midday bounce had no clear catalyst, while the late -6.4 pip dip was tied to Treasury Secretary Bessent's USD-positive remarks.

polarity_reads.read: Unscored, but the +0.044% USD impulse and high-sigma USD/CHF (+3.35) and USD/CAD (+2.4) reactions suggest the market was positioned for USD-positive policy talk rather than trading a specific data surprise.
Muted despite a 27.8K vs 8.3K miss with GBP basket only -0.029%, inside the noise floor; implies the weak UK jobs print was already expected or the broad USD/oil tape dominated the UK data shock.

scenarios.name: US retail strength extends dollar bid
scenarios.thesis: Firm US retail sales validate today's USD strength, extending USD/JPY and USD/CHF gains while EUR/USD and GBP/USD fade late-session support.
triggers: US Core Retail Sales m/m prints at or above 0.5%
US Retail Sales m/m prints at or above 0.8%
Bessent follow-through remains USD-positive and oil headlines do not trigger risk-off
scenarios.invalidation: Weak US retail sales or UK CPI above 3.1% triggers a sharp GBP/USD reversal. A risk-off oil spike could also reverse USD/JPY.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD range was 34.0 pips today; the Bessent reaction already produced -3.3 pips in 15 min, so an extension targets the lower end of that range.
USD/JPY closed up 74.8 pips on the day; JPY's -0.282% weakness and broad USD strength support a retest of the high.
USD/CHF range was 44.5 pips; the Bessent reaction showed +5.0 pips in 15 min at 3.35 sigma, pointing to continued CHF underperformance.

scenarios.name: Oil supply shock keeps CAD supported and high-beta FX weak
scenarios.thesis: Saudi cargo cancellations and Strait of Hormuz headlines keep Brent bid and CAD underpinned, while NZD and JPY remain laggards against a mixed USD.
triggers: Further confirmation of Saudi cargo cancellations or East-West pipeline outage
Brent holds near 110.594, its close at 0.99 in range
US retail sales are not too strong
scenarios.invalidation: De-escalation headlines, a sharp increase in US retail sales, or a strong USD bid from Bessent follow-through.

pair_paths.rationale: USD/CAD range was 31.6 pips; the Saudi headline produced a -17.2 pip down leg with an in-leg driver of -6.6 pips, so oil support can retest the lows.
NZD/USD range was 37.1 pips; NZD is -0.236% weak and oil-risk headlines pressure high-beta currencies.
USD/JPY traded a 124.5-pip range today; oil headlines create two-way flow, but the bias is not clear enough for a breakout.

scenarios.name: GBP CPI surprise lifts GBP and triggers USD pullback
scenarios.thesis: A strong UK CPI forces a repricing of GBP, pulling EUR/GBP lower and GBP/USD higher, while soft US retail sales adds to a USD unwind.
triggers: US Retail Sales m/m misses its 0.8% forecast
JPY reverses some of its -0.282% weakness
scenarios.invalidation: CPI at or below 3.1% and strong US data support USD; risk-off oil headlines could also disrupt the GBP rebound.

pair_paths.rationale: GBP/USD range was 49.4 pips; GBP +0.064% strength today despite muted jobs data shows room to catch up on a strong CPI.
EUR/GBP range was 15.0 pips; a hot UK CPI likely pushes EUR/GBP toward the low end of that range.
USD/JPY closed up 74.8 pips on the day, but a USD unwind can retrace that move; JPY is the weakest major, but a risk-off reaction may reverse the late US bid.

risks.risk: Strait of Hormuz / oil supply escalation
risks.why_it_matters: Brent/USD closed +2.752% near highs; further disruptions can spike oil and support CAD/NOK while pressuring high-beta FX.
risks.watch: Iranian military claims, Oman-US de-escalation talks, Saudi cargo cancellations

risks.why_it_matters: Core Retail Sales m/m forecast 0.5% vs previous -0.3% and Retail Sales m/m 0.8% vs -0.6%; firm prints would validate today's USD strength, weak prints unwind it.
risks.watch: US Core Retail Sales m/m and Retail Sales m/m at 14:30

risks.why_it_matters: GBP CPI y/y forecast 3.1% vs previous 2.9%; a hot print can lift GBP and pressure EUR/GBP, conflicting with the USD bid.
risks.watch: UK CPI y/y at 08:00 and any core/service detail

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: UK CPI y/y (forecast 3.1%, prev 2.9%) at 08:00 can lift GBP if hot, while US Core Retail Sales m/m (0.5% vs -0.3%) and Retail Sales m/m (0.8% vs -0.6%) at 14:30 will validate or break the day's USD strength.
